quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction, Basic Tags, Attributes & Global Attributes.

questions.prompt: Which element holds the visible content of an HTML page?
questions.explanation: The <head> holds information about the page (title, meta tags). Everything the user sees goes inside <body>.

questions.prompt: What is the alt attribute of an for?
options: Adding a border around the image
Linking the image to another page
Setting the width of the image
Text for screen readers and for when the image cannot load
questions.explanation: alt describes the image in words. Screen readers read it aloud and browsers show it if the file fails to load.

questions.prompt: Which attribute must be unique on a page?
questions.explanation: An id identifies exactly one element. Many elements can share the same class, title or lang.

questions.prompt: What does the browser show for this code?
options: The tags are printed as plain text
A paragraph where only the word HTML is bold
Nothing, because strong is not a valid tag
questions.explanation: <strong> only affects the text between its own opening and closing tags.

questions.prompt: What happens when a user clicks this link?
options: example.com opens in a new tab
example.com opens in the same tab
questions.explanation: target="_blank" tells the browser to open the link in a new tab or window.

questions.prompt: Complete the tag so the text becomes a top-level heading.
questions.explanation: h1 is the main (top-level) heading. The closing tag shows which element this is.

quizzes.title: Structure & Content Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Semantic & Non-Semantic, Div, Span & Lists.

questions.prompt: Which element is the most meaningful choice for the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> tells browsers and screen readers that this block contains navigation links.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between <div> and <span>?
options: span is a block element, div is inline
div is a block element, span is inline
They are identical in every way
questions.explanation: A div starts on a new line and takes the full width. A span stays inside the line of text.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates an ordered (numbered) list?
questions.explanation: <ol> is the ordered list. <ul> is bulleted, <li> is a single item and <dl> is a description list.

questions.prompt: How many bullet points appear in total?
questions.explanation: Every <li> is a bullet: Fruits, the nested Apple, and Bread.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with using <div> for every part of a page?
options: It makes the page load slower
Screen readers and search engines cannot tell what each part means
questions.explanation: div has no meaning. Semantic elements like header, nav, main and footer describe the role of each part.

questions.prompt: Complete the tag for the page footer.
questions.explanation: footer is the semantic element for closing information such as copyright.

quizzes.title: Tables & Forms Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Table & Form, Forms in Depth & Validation.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a table row?
questions.explanation: tr is a table row. td is a data cell and th is a header cell inside the row.

questions.prompt: How do you connect a <label> to its input?
options: Put the label after the input
Give the label a for attribute that matches the input's id
questions.explanation: for="email" on the label and id="email" on the input link them, so clicking the label focuses the input.

questions.prompt: Which input attribute stops the form from being sent when the field is empty?
questions.explanation: required makes the browser block submission and show a message until the field is filled.

questions.prompt: A user types "sara" (no @) and presses Submit. What happens?
options: The browser changes it to sara@gmail.com
The browser blocks the submit and shows an error message
questions.explanation: type="email" makes the browser check the format before the form is submitted.

questions.prompt: Why must the server validate form data even though the browser already does?
options: Browser checks can be bypassed by anyone
questions.explanation: Anyone can edit the page or send a request directly. Only server-side checks can be trusted.

questions.prompt: Complete the attribute so only one radio button of the group can be chosen.
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name form one group, and only one of them can be selected.

questions.prompt: How many <h1> elements should a page normally have?
questions.explanation: One h1 describes the main topic of the page. Use h2, h3 and so on for the sections below it.

questions.prompt: What is the best alt text for a purely decorative image?
questions.explanation: An empty alt tells screen readers to skip the image, so users are not bothered by it.

questions.prompt: Which link text is best for accessibility?
questions.explanation: Link text should make sense on its own, because screen reader users often jump from link to link.

questions.prompt: What is this tag for?
options: Making the page display properly on phones
Adding a title to the browser tab
Setting the language of the page
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers to use the real device width instead of a zoomed-out desktop width.

questions.prompt: Which element sets the text shown on the browser tab?
questions.explanation: <title> inside <head> is used for the tab text and is also important for search results.

questions.prompt: Complete the attribute that sets the language of the page.
questions.explanation: lang helps screen readers pronounce the content correctly and helps search engines.
